questions.stem: Which is the most dangerous type of cervical spinal injury?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Hyperextension injury
Hyperextension is much more dangerous in causing spinal damage. It is because the weak anterior longitudinal ligament is incapable of preserving the integrity of the cervical spine during hyperextension.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man presents with complaints of constipation, abdominal cramps, and tingling in the extremities. His bloodwork shows a lead level of 50 µg/dL. What is the antidote preferred for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

DMSA

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of lead poisoning. Calcium EDTA and DMSA (succimer) are the preferred antidotes for lead poisoning.

questions.stem: To detect vaginal cells on a person who is accused of rape, which test will you use?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

Lugol’s

Lugol’s iodine test will be used to detect the vaginal cells present on the penis of a rape accused. It shows brown color on filter paper due to the presence of glycogen in epithelial cells of the vagina.

questions.stem: A deceased man is being evaluated for suspected poisoning. During an autopsy, you get a peculiar garlicky smell from the nose and mouth of the body. Which of the following agents would you suspect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

Phosphorus
This scenario is suggestive of phosphorus poisoning as it is associated with a garlic-like odor, usually around the mouth and nose of the victim. Other substances associated with a garlic-like odor are arsenic, thallium carbonate, and zinc phosphide.

questions.stem: Which is the most common intracranial lesion due to head injury?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

Cerebral contusion
The most common type of intracranial lesion following trauma is cerebral contusion.

questions.stem: A woman gave birth to twins. Although a detailed evaluation revealed the same gestational age, the father believed that the children did not belong to him and requested DNA testing. After testing, it was found that one child did not belong to him. What is this case best described as?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Superfecundation

The given clinical scenario where twins have different fathers is suggestive of heteropaternal superfecundation.

questions.stem: Which chelating agent is not used in heavy metal poisoning?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

Pralidoxime
Pralidoxime is used in organophosphate poisoning and not as a chelator in heavy metal poisoning.

questions.stem: As per the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 2021, induction of MTP in a mentally ill or a rape victim is allowed until what age of gestation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

24 weeks
As per the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021, the induction of MTP in a mentally ill woman or a rape victim is allowed until 24 weeks.

questions.stem: Suspended animation can occur in all of the following conditions except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)        

Throttling
Suspended animation is not seen in throttling (manual strangulation). Suspended animation is a condition where signs of life are absent as functions are interrupted for some time or are reduced to a minimum.

questions.stem: The police hands over the body of a person who died due to hanging to you for an autopsy. Which of the following incisions is preferred in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Modified Y shaped incision
The incision preferred in the case of asphyxial death due to neck compression (as in hanging) is the modified Y-shaped incision.

questions.stem: A boy was taken away from his guardian without his guardian’s consent. This will constitute as ‘kidnapping’ in India if the boy’s age is under:
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

16 years
Taking away the male child below the age of 16 years without the consent of his guardian constitutes kidnapping.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a feature of cocaine intoxication?

options.label: A
options.text: Tingling and numbness of hands and feet

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Constricted pupils and bradycardia
Constricted pupils and bradycardia are not a feature of cocaine intoxication. Dilated pupils and rapid pulse are seen in cocaine intoxication.

questions.stem: A pregnant woman suffered a miscarriage at 6 months of gestation. What would be the expected crown heel length of this fetus?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

30 cm 
Crown heel length of a 6-month-old fetus would be 30 cm.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man was using mushrooms for recreational purposes. On one of his bad days, he overdosed on them and presented to ER with symptoms of poisoning. What is the drug of choice for this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Atropine
The drug of choice for mushroom poisoning is atropine. Atropine is of no value in the delayed onset of mushroom poisoning that occurs after ingestion of Amanita phyllodes.

questions.stem: A pregnant female comes to a gynaecologist, who sends her for USG. On USG, twin pregnancy was noted with about a one-month difference in the age of fetuses. Which of the following is true with regard to this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Superfetation

The above phenomenon is known as superfetation. It occurs when there is fertilization of 2 different ova released in different menstrual cycles. The consequence is two children are born at the same time and one of them might be mature while another might be immature or two fully developed fetuses are born at intervals ranging from one to three months apart.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old fisherman was brought dead. His autopsy findings revealed emphysema aquosum. What is the most probable cause of death?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Wet drowning
Emphysema aquosum is seen in cases of wet drowning. Overinflation of the lungs in drowning is known as emphysema aquosum. It is one of the most valuable positive signs of drowning.

questions.stem: Which of the following poison can be found even in skeletonised remains of the body?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Arsenic

Arsenic can be found even in skeletonized remains of the body.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common sign seen in patients undergoing alcohol withdrawal?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Tremors
Tremors/Tremulousness or shakes’ or ‘jitters’ is the most common sign of alcohol withdrawal. This occurs about 12- 24 hours after their last drink.

questions.stem: A female was brought for autopsy with an alleged history of being found at a lake in the village. All of the following are suggestive of antemortem drowning except:

options.label: C
options.text: White leathery foam around mouth and nostrils

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Washerwoman’s hands and feet
Washerwoman’s hands and feet are a non-specific sign of submersion. They occur due to the imbibition of water into the outer skin layers. They can be seen in antemortem as well as postmortem drowning victims. The presence of water in the stomach, white leathery foam around the mouth and nostrils, and a positive diatom test are suggestive of antemortem drowning.
